title: Evaluating agents as evolving systems
dek: A practical evaluation loop for agents that change with prompts, tools, and model upgrades.

stories.title: Google describes a hill-climbing workflow for agent evaluation
stories.dek: The unit of improvement is the complete agent system, not an isolated model score.
stories.evidence: Vendor engineering walkthrough; not independent results
stories.takeaway: Track full traces and per-case outcomes on a frozen regression set. Do not promote a model or prompt change based only on a mean score.

bullets.detail: Google's Agents CLI separates trace generation, grading, run comparisons, failure analysis, and prompt optimization; the unit of evaluation is the tool-using agent, not the model alone.
A system-prompt edit can suppress tool calls and produce unsupported answers while the application code still executes.
Across four test cases, mean response-quality score dropped from 4.00 to 2.75 / 5 after a prompt regression.
Four examples illustrate the regression-detection workflow; they are insufficient to estimate production reliability.
Freeze representative financial retrieval, numerical reconciliation, citations, entitlement checks, and structured-query tasks.
Compare per-case tool traces, task success, unsupported claims, unauthorized actions, p95 latency, and cost. Reject regressions masked by a stable mean.

sources.name: Google Developers Blog - Hill-Climbing Agent Quality with Agents CLI Evaluation

stories.title: A2UI Express separates UI generation from rendering
stories.dek: Google introduces a compact inference format that compiles into validated A2UI messages, reducing model output while keeping rendering under client control.
stories.evidence: Google vendor measurements; independent replication pending
stories.takeaway: Prototype A2UI Express against direct JSON on representative financial workflows. Measure end-to-end latency, valid render rate, authorization checks and correction cost before selecting a generation format.

bullets.detail: The client supplies a catalog of allowed UI components. The agent proposes a component tree; the client renders validated structures rather than executing model-generated interface code.
The model emits compact, line-oriented output. The SDK deterministically compiles the full response to validated A2UI messages; the component catalog and renderer stay unchanged.
Catalog constraints restrict UI structures, not the truth of displayed values or permission to execute actions. Server-side entitlements and data provenance remain separate controls.
Google reports up to 3× fewer output tokens and up to 3× lower latency versus Direct JSON; its comparison spans 51 tasks with gemini-3.5-flash under different thinking settings.
Direct JSON can stream chunks; Express waits for the full response before compilation. Faster completion does not guarantee earlier first useful render.

Google separately cites up to 80× faster layout decisions with Jev. An 11-prompt demonstration reported 92–298 ms component trees and 0.8–1.7 s complete screens; this is not an independent Express comparison.
Published figures are vendor measurements, not independently replicated production latency, cost, correctness, or security results. Jev's format is not yet included in the cited SDKs.
Run 50–100 representative document, market-data, alert, and research tasks with the same model, catalog, and backend; compare Direct JSON with Express.

Measure p50/p95 end-to-end time, first useful render, token cost, valid renders, missing fields, retries, and denied-action behavior. Only promote when correctness and authorization meet baseline thresholds.

sources.name: Google Developers Blog - Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats
